reason: This passage (1 Samuel 18-20) describes the covenant of loyalty and friendship between David and Jonathan. While it portrays Saul's violent acts—including attempting to kill David and casting a spear at Jonathan—these actions are presented negatively as products of jealousy and paranoia, not as legitimate leadership models. David is not portrayed as 'unruly'; rather, he is loyal and obedient. The text explicitly praises Jonathan's defense of David against his father's violence and celebrates their covenant bond of love and mutual protection. The ethical model presented is one of righteous loyalty and covenant friendship, not violence as a leadership tool.
